words.enDefinition: A full-length film that can be shown as the main presentation.

examples.en: The campus festival showed a feature film after three shorts made by local students.
examples.zh: 校园影展放了三部本地学生制作的短片，接着放了一部「长篇电影」。

examples.en: My classmate had never watched a feature film in a theater before coming to university.
examples.zh: 来上大学之前，同学从没在影院看过「长篇电影」。

words.enDefinition: A film much shorter than a typical feature film.

examples.en: We watched a short film before the director came out to answer our questions.
examples.zh: 导演出来回答问题前，我们看了一部「电影短片」。

examples.en: My roommate made a short film about the people who work in our library.
examples.zh: 室友拍了一部关于图书馆工作人员的「电影短片」。

words.enDefinition: Made primarily by filming real performers and settings instead of animating the action.

examples.en: I liked how the live-action film made the setting feel like a real neighborhood.
examples.zh: 我喜欢这部「真人实拍的」电影把故事发生地拍得像真实的街区。

examples.en: The poster showed which characters would appear in the live-action adaptation of the book.
examples.zh: 海报展示了这本书改编成「真人实拍」电影后会出现哪些角色。

words.enDefinition: A full-length film that tells its story mainly through animation.

examples.en: An animated feature played at the campus cinema before the director's talk on Friday.
examples.zh: 星期五导演座谈前，校园影院放了一部「动画长片」。

examples.en: I picked an animated feature because my roommate was interested in the film's visual style.
examples.zh: 我选了部「动画长片」，因为室友对它的视觉风格感兴趣。

words.enDefinition: Animation made by photographing objects in slightly different positions frame by frame.

examples.en: The short used stop-motion animation to make a desk lamp look like it could walk.
examples.zh: 这部短片用「定格动画」让台灯看起来像会走路。

examples.en: We saw a display about stop-motion animation beside the costumes at the campus film exhibition.
examples.zh: 在校园电影展上，我们在戏服旁边看到了介绍「定格动画」的展品。

words.enDefinition: A film or program that explores real people, events, or subjects.

examples.en: We watched a documentary about the volunteers who run a small library after school.
examples.zh: 我们看了一部「纪录片」，讲的是放学后帮忙经营小图书馆的志愿者。

examples.en: The documentary made me curious about what happens after our old textbooks get donated.
examples.zh: 这部「纪录片」让我好奇，旧教材捐出去以后会怎样。

words.enDefinition: A fictional film or show made to look like a documentary, often for comedy.

examples.en: The mockumentary followed a fictional library team trying to run its first book fair.
examples.zh: 这部「伪纪录片」跟拍了一个虚构的图书馆团队，讲他们如何办第一次书展。

examples.en: I realized it was a mockumentary when the supposed experts started contradicting each other.
examples.zh: 所谓的专家们开始互相拆台，我才意识到这是部「伪纪录片」。

words.enDefinition: A set of documentary episodes about related people, events, or subjects.

examples.en: We started a docuseries about city parks after our tutor mentioned it in class.
examples.zh: 导师上课提过一部城市公园题材的「纪录片剧集」，我们就开始看了。

examples.en: Each episode of the docuseries followed a different team working in the same museum.
examples.zh: 这部「纪录片剧集」每集跟拍在同一家博物馆工作的不同团队。

words.enDefinition: A dramatized film about the life of a real person.

examples.en: The biopic focused on the musician's early years and only briefly showed her first major tour.
examples.zh: 这部「人物传记片」主要讲这位音乐人的早年，第一次大型巡演只是一笔带过。

examples.en: We compared the biopic with an interview the subject gave near the end of his career.
examples.zh: 我们把这部「人物传记片」和片中人物职业生涯末期的一次访谈作了比较。

words.enDefinition: A drama set in a past historical period and portraying life from that time.

examples.en: We chose a period drama because my classmate wanted to see the clothes and interiors.
examples.zh: 我们选了一部「年代剧」，因为同学想看里面的服装和室内陈设。

examples.en: The period drama was set in a village at a time before cars were common.
examples.zh: 这部「年代剧」的故事发生在一个村子里，那时汽车还不普及。

collocations: a costume from a period drama
a period drama set in the seventies

words.enDefinition: A film about a young person growing into a more mature self.

examples.en: The coming-of-age film followed a student figuring out what to do after leaving home.
examples.zh: 这部「成长题材电影」讲的是一名学生离开家后如何摸索接下来的路。

examples.en: My roommate called it a coming-of-age film about finding your place in a new city.
examples.zh: 室友说这是一部「成长题材电影」，讲的是如何在新城市找到自己的位置。

collocations: a coming-of-age film set in a small town

words.enDefinition: A humorous film or show about people falling in love or navigating a relationship.

examples.en: We felt like watching a romantic comedy after spending the afternoon finishing our final projects.
examples.zh: 下午把期末项目做完后，我们想看一部「浪漫喜剧」。

examples.en: The romantic comedy was funnier when it showed the couple making ordinary mistakes together.
examples.zh: 这部「浪漫喜剧」里，两人一起犯日常小错误的片段更好笑。

words.enDefinition: Comedy that finds humor in serious, unpleasant, or disturbing situations.

examples.en: The dark comedy made the scholarship interview funny without making it seem any less stressful.
examples.zh: 这部「黑色喜剧」把奖学金面试拍得好笑，面试的紧张感也还在。

examples.en: I wasn't expecting the dark comedy to make me laugh at such an awkward scene.
examples.zh: 没想到这部「黑色喜剧」会让我在那种尴尬的场面笑出来。

collocations: a dark comedy about office life
describe a film as a dark comedy

words.enDefinition: A comedy series built around recurring characters and the situations they regularly get into.

examples.en: My flatmate put on a sitcom set in a small radio station downtown.
examples.zh: 室友放了一部「情景喜剧」，故事发生在市中心一家小电台。

examples.en: The situation comedy used the same handful of characters even when the location changed.
examples.zh: 这部「情景喜剧」切换场景时，出场的还是同样那几个人。

words.enDefinition: Fiction that imagines developments in science, technology, or the worlds they might shape.

examples.en: I usually watch science fiction for the ideas about technology rather than the space settings.
examples.zh: 我看「科幻题材」作品，通常更关注里面对技术的想象。

examples.en: The science fiction series imagined a future where people could share memories with friends.
examples.zh: 这部「科幻题材」剧集想象在未来人们能和朋友分享记忆。

words.enDefinition: A film in which magic, imaginary creatures, or impossible worlds are central to the story.

examples.en: The fantasy film took place in a city where buildings moved during the night.
examples.zh: 这部「奇幻电影」的故事发生在一座城市里，城里的建筑会在夜间移动。

examples.en: My classmate wanted to know how the fantasy film had created its unusual creatures.
examples.zh: 同学想知道这部「奇幻电影」里那些不寻常的生物是怎么设计出来的。

collocations: a fantasy film set in another world

words.enDefinition: A thriller that builds suspense through characters' fears, perceptions, or mental conflict.

examples.en: The psychological thriller left me wondering which of the main character's memories I could trust.
examples.zh: 这部「心理惊悚片」让我一直想，主角的哪些回忆才可信。

examples.en: We picked a psychological thriller because the description suggested a story built around uncertainty.
examples.zh: 故事简介说情节围绕不确定性展开，我们就选了这部「心理惊悚片」。

collocations: the ending of a psychological thriller

words.enDefinition: A film intended to frighten or unsettle viewers.

examples.en: I watched the horror film with both lights on while my roommate finished her work.
examples.zh: 室友忙着把工作做完时，我开了两盏灯看这部「恐怖电影」。

examples.en: The horror film was unsettling mostly because we could hear things we couldn't see.
examples.zh: 这部「恐怖电影」让人不安，主要是因为能听见动静，却看不见是什么。

words.enDefinition: A series centered on discovering the answer to a puzzling event or question.

examples.en: We started a mystery series about a box of letters found under a floorboard.
examples.zh: 我们开始看一部「悬疑推理剧集」，故事从地板下发现一盒信件讲起。

examples.en: The mystery series made our flatmates argue about which small details would matter later.
examples.zh: 这部「悬疑推理剧集」让我们室友争论哪些小细节之后会派上用场。

words.enDefinition: A fictional drama centered on a crime, its investigation, or people affected by it.

examples.en: The crime drama spent most of its time on the people affected by the investigation.
examples.zh: 这部「犯罪题材剧」把主要篇幅放在受调查影响的人身上。

examples.en: My roommate likes a crime drama with a believable detective and a convincing setting.
examples.zh: 室友喜欢侦探人物真实、场景也可信的「犯罪题材剧」。

words.enDefinition: A film or show that combines fast-paced action with comic situations.

examples.en: The action comedy made us laugh most when the characters tried to work together.
examples.zh: 这部「动作喜剧」里，角色们试着合作的那段最让我们发笑。

examples.en: We put on an action comedy because everyone wanted something energetic after a quiet afternoon.
examples.zh: 下午安安静静过完后，大家想看点热闹的，我们就放了部「动作喜剧」。

words.enDefinition: A film made without recorded dialogue synchronized to what happens on screen.

examples.en: The campus cinema showed a silent film with live piano music on Friday evening.
examples.zh: 星期五晚上，校园影院放了一部「无声电影」，有钢琴现场配乐。

examples.en: We studied a silent film that conveyed an awkward reunion entirely through expressions and gestures.
examples.zh: 我们分析了一部「无声电影」，片中一次尴尬的重逢全靠表情和动作来表现。

collocations: live music for a silent film

words.enDefinition: A program following real participants in filmed situations, challenges, or daily activities.

examples.en: The reality show followed students trying to redesign a shared space in their building.
examples.zh: 这档「真人秀节目」跟拍了一群尝试改造楼里共用空间的学生。

examples.en: My roommate likes a reality show where teams design things under a time limit.
examples.zh: 室友爱看一种「真人秀节目」，各队要在规定时间内完成设计。

collocations: take part in a reality show

words.enDefinition: A program where contestants play games, answer questions, or compete for prizes.

examples.en: We guessed the answers together while a game show played in the residence lounge.
examples.zh: 宿舍休息室播着一档「电视竞赛节目」，我们就一起猜答案。

examples.en: The game show asked contestants to recognize songs from only the first few notes.
examples.zh: 这档「电视竞赛节目」要求参赛者只听开头几个音就认出歌曲。

collocations: a contestant on a game show

words.enDefinition: A program in which a host talks with guests about their lives or work.

examples.en: I saw the director on a talk show explaining how the film came together.
examples.zh: 我看到导演在一档「访谈节目」里介绍这部电影是怎么拍出来的。

examples.en: The talk show featured a guest who had turned a campus project into a documentary.
examples.zh: 这档「访谈节目」邀请了一位把校园项目拍成纪录片的嘉宾。

collocations: a guest on a talk show

words.enDefinition: Comedy presented as a series of separate short comic scenes.

examples.en: The streaming service listed the show under sketch comedy because each scene had different characters.
examples.zh: 每场戏角色各不相同，所以流媒体平台把这档节目列在「短剧喜剧」下面。

examples.en: A friend likes sketch comedy because one funny scene is easy to watch between classes.
examples.zh: 有位朋友喜欢「短剧喜剧」，因为课间看一个搞笑场景很方便。

words.enDefinition: A series planned as a finite set of episodes that tells a complete story.

examples.en: We picked a limited series because the main story would be finished after six episodes.
examples.zh: 我们选了部「限定剧」，因为主线情节六集就会讲完。

examples.en: The review said the limited series gave the characters more time than a film would.
examples.zh: 影评说，这部「限定剧」比电影有更多篇幅来塑造人物。

collocations: a limited series based on a novel

words.enDefinition: A series that tells separate stories in individual episodes or groups of episodes.

examples.en: Each episode of the anthology series took place in a different apartment building downtown.
examples.zh: 这部「独立故事式剧集」每集的故事都发生在市中心不同的公寓楼里。

examples.en: I liked that the anthology series could change its cast completely from one season to another.
examples.zh: 我喜欢这部「独立故事式剧集」各季能够换一批全新的演员。

collocations: an anthology series with a shared theme

words.enDefinition: An episode with a self-contained story that viewers can follow without seeing the others.

examples.en: My roommate recommended a stand-alone episode because I had missed the rest of the season.
examples.zh: 室友推荐了「剧情独立的一集」，因为我没看这一季的其他集。

examples.en: We finished a stand-alone episode while waiting for another friend to get back from class.
examples.zh: 我们等另一位朋友下课回来时，看完了「剧情独立的一集」。

words.enDefinition: An initial episode made to introduce or test the idea for a potential series.

examples.en: The pilot episode introduced three students sharing a kitchen in a new residence hall.
examples.zh: 「试播集」介绍了三个在新宿舍共用厨房的学生。

examples.en: We compared the pilot episode with the later show to see what the writers changed.
examples.zh: 我们把「试播集」和后来的正式剧集作了比较，看看编剧改了哪些地方。

collocations: cast members in the pilot episode

words.enDefinition: The first episode of a particular season of a television series.

examples.en: The season opener introduced a new classmate before returning to the story from last year.
examples.zh: 「新一季首集」先介绍了一位新同学，才接着讲去年的情节。

examples.en: My flatmates saved the season opener to watch together when everyone returned from break.
examples.zh: 室友们把「新一季首集」留着，等大家放假回来再一起看。

words.enDefinition: The final episode in a season of a television series.

examples.en: The season finale answered one question but left us guessing what would happen next.
examples.zh: 「一季的最后一集」解答了一个疑问，却又让我们猜接下来会发生什么。

examples.en: We saved the season finale for Friday because nobody could stay up late that night.
examples.zh: 那晚谁都不能熬夜，我们就把「一季的最后一集」留到星期五再看。

collocations: a surprise in the season finale

words.enDefinition: The last episode of an entire television show, in North American usage.

examples.en: We watched the series finale together after following the show since our first year.
examples.zh: 我们从大一开始追这部剧，最后一起看了「整部剧的最终集」。

examples.en: The series finale showed where several of the characters ended up after leaving town.
examples.zh: 「整部剧的最终集」讲了几位角色离开小镇后各有怎样的去向。

words.enDefinition: The central situation or idea on which a story is built.

examples.en: The story premise sounded ordinary until I learned that the whole plot happened in one day.
examples.zh: 后来我才知道整个情节都发生在一天内，先前还觉得这个「故事基本设定」很普通。

examples.en: My roommate liked the story premise but thought the opening could have been shorter.
examples.zh: 室友喜欢这个「故事基本设定」，不过觉得开头可以更短一些。

collocations: a story premise for a film

words.enDefinition: The sequence of events forming a story or a thread within it.

examples.en: I could follow the storyline even though I had missed the first few minutes.
examples.zh: 虽然错过了开头几分钟，我还是能跟上「故事线」。

examples.en: The storyline about the sisters kept me watching after the campus scenes began to repeat.
examples.zh: 后来校园里一些场景开始重复，但姐妹俩的「故事线」让我继续看了下去。

collocations: bring a storyline to an end

words.enDefinition: A secondary story running alongside the main plot.

examples.en: The subplot about the missing notebook was funnier than the main story for me.
examples.zh: 对我来说，丢笔记本的「支线情节」比主线故事还好笑。

examples.en: The film dropped a subplot from the book to spend more time with the family.
examples.zh: 电影删掉了书里的一段「支线情节」，把更多篇幅留给了这一家人。

words.enDefinition: The course of a character's development or change across a story.

examples.en: Her character arc made sense once we saw how she handled the final setback.
examples.zh: 看到她怎么应对最后一次挫折，我们就理解了她的「角色变化轨迹」。

examples.en: Our film club discussed the character arc of the quietest person in the story.
examples.zh: 我们电影社讨论了故事里最沉默的那个人的「角色变化轨迹」。

words.enDefinition: A group of actors who share the major roles in a story.

examples.en: The series used an ensemble cast, so each episode could follow a different roommate.
examples.zh: 这部剧采用「群像阵容」，所以每集都可以跟着不同的室友展开。

examples.en: My classmate liked the ensemble cast because even minor stories were given time to develop.
examples.zh: 同学喜欢这部戏的「群像阵容」，因为连小故事都有足够的展开篇幅。

words.enDefinition: A central acting part in a film, show, or play.

examples.en: I recognized the actor in the lead role from a short film our class watched.
examples.zh: 我认出这位扮演「主要角色」的演员在我们班看过的短片里演过。

examples.en: She got her first lead role in a low-budget feature made near her university.
examples.zh: 她第一次担任「主要角色」，是在学校附近拍的一部长篇低成本电影里。

collocations: cast someone in the lead role

words.enDefinition: An acting part that is less central than the lead but contributes to the story.

examples.en: My favorite actor had a supporting role as the librarian who remembered everyone's name.
examples.zh: 我最喜欢的演员演的是「配角」，那位记得每个人名字的图书管理员。

examples.en: One student thought the actor in a supporting role should have had more scenes.
examples.zh: 有位同学觉得演「配角」的那位演员应该多几场戏。

collocations: cast someone in a supporting role

words.enDefinition: The first scene in a film or an episode.

examples.en: The opening scene showed an empty lecture hall before any of the characters appeared.
examples.zh: 角色出场前，「开场戏」先拍了一间空的阶梯教室。

examples.en: I had to explain the opening scene when my roommate got home from work.
examples.zh: 室友下班回家时，我得跟她讲一下「开场戏」演了什么。

collocations: set the opening scene in a library

words.enDefinition: The names of the people and organizations involved in a production shown at the end.

examples.en: We stayed for the closing credits because my classmate's sister had worked on the film.
examples.zh: 同学的姐姐参与过这部片，我们就留下来看了「片尾演职员表」。

examples.en: The song over the closing credits sounded familiar, but I could not remember its title.
examples.zh: 「片尾演职员表」出现时放的歌听着耳熟，不过我想不起歌名。

collocations: a song over the closing credits

words.enDefinition: An extra scene shown after the main credits at the end of a production.

examples.en: We waited for the post-credits scene after everyone else had left the screening room.
examples.zh: 其他人都离开放映厅后，我们还在等「片尾字幕后附加场景」。

examples.en: The post-credits scene showed the two friends finally returning the books they had borrowed.
examples.zh: 「片尾字幕后附加场景」里，两位朋友终于把借的书还了回去。

words.enDefinition: A scene that goes back to something which happened earlier in the story's timeline.

examples.en: The flashback explained how the two neighbors had met long before the main story began.
examples.zh: 「闪回」说明，在主线故事开始很久之前，两位邻居是怎么认识的。

examples.en: I missed a short flashback while I was making tea and had to ask about it.
examples.zh: 泡茶时我错过了一小段「闪回」，只好问刚才演了什么。

collocations: tell a story through a flashback

words.enDefinition: A scene that jumps ahead to something later in the story's timeline.

examples.en: The episode began with a flash-forward to the main character's last day at school.
examples.zh: 这一集开头用「闪前」，先演了主角在学校的最后一天。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether the flash-forward changed how we understood the events at the start.
examples.zh: 导师问，这段「闪前」有没有改变我们对开头那些事件的理解。

words.enDefinition: A story told outside the chronological order in which the events happen.

examples.en: The nonlinear narrative moved between three points in the same family's history without warning.
examples.zh: 这部片用「非线性叙事」，在同一个家庭的三个历史阶段之间切换，没有事先提示。

examples.en: I enjoyed the nonlinear narrative more once I stopped trying to arrange every scene by date.
examples.zh: 我不再试着按日期排每场戏之后，反而更喜欢这种「非线性叙事」了。

collocations: make sense of a nonlinear narrative
a film with a nonlinear narrative

words.enDefinition: An unexpected development that changes the direction or meaning of the story.

examples.en: I guessed the plot twist when the same postcard appeared in two different rooms.
examples.zh: 同一张明信片出现在两个房间里时，我猜到了「剧情反转」。

examples.en: The plot twist made us rethink a scene we had laughed at near the beginning.
examples.zh: 这个「剧情反转」让我们重新理解开头那场曾逗我们笑的戏。

words.enDefinition: An ending that leaves an important event unresolved so viewers want to know what happens next.

examples.en: The episode ended on a cliffhanger just as the main character was about to read the letter.
examples.zh: 主角刚要读信，这一集就用了个「悬念式结尾」。

examples.en: We complained about the cliffhanger because the next episode would not arrive until the following week.
examples.zh: 下一集得等到下周才出，我们就抱怨这个「悬念式结尾」。

words.enDefinition: Information that reveals an important event that a viewer might want to discover for themselves.

examples.en: I saw a spoiler while looking up the name of one of the actors.
examples.zh: 我查其中一位演员的名字时看到了一条「剧透」。

examples.en: The first paragraph of the review had a spoiler for anyone who missed the finale.
examples.zh: 对还没看终集的人来说，影评第一段里就有「剧透」。

words.enDefinition: A warning that the next part of a discussion reveals an important story detail.

examples.en: The reviewer gave a spoiler alert before talking about the last scene in detail.
examples.zh: 影评人在细讲最后一场戏之前先发了个「剧透提醒」。

examples.en: My classmate put a spoiler alert above her message about what happened in the episode.
examples.zh: 同学发消息聊这一集演了什么前，先在上面写了「剧透提醒」。

collocations: a spoiler alert before the review

words.enDefinition: A request to avoid revealing important events, often because someone has not watched yet.

examples.en: “No spoilers,” I said when my roommates started talking about the episode over breakfast.
examples.zh: 室友们吃早餐时聊起那一集，我就说「别剧透」。

examples.en: I wrote “No spoilers” in the chat because half the group had missed the screening.
examples.zh: 有一半组员没赶上放映，我就在群里写了「别剧透」。

collocations: say no spoilers before a discussion

words.enDefinition: A narrator whose account may be inaccurate, selective, or misleading.

examples.en: The unreliable narrator kept leaving out details that turned out to matter later on.
examples.zh: 这个「不可靠叙述者」总漏掉一些细节，后来才知道都很关键。

examples.en: Our class discussed whether the unreliable narrator had misunderstood events or was hiding something.
examples.zh: 我们班讨论那个「不可靠叙述者」是误解了发生的事，还是有所隐瞒。

collocations: a story with an unreliable narrator

words.enDefinition: Speech heard over a scene without the speaker visibly saying it on screen.

examples.en: The voice-over read part of a letter while the camera showed the empty house.
examples.zh: 镜头里是空房子，「画外音」念了一段信里的内容。

examples.en: I recognized the voice-over because the same actor had appeared in a show last term.
examples.zh: 上学期看过同一个演员演的剧，我就认出了这段「画外音」是谁配的。

collocations: use a voice-over in the opening scene

words.enDefinition: A gap or inconsistency in the story that makes part of it difficult to believe.

examples.en: My roommate noticed a plot hole when the train arrived before the station had opened.
examples.zh: 火车在车站开门前就到了，室友看出了一个「情节漏洞」。

examples.en: We spent more time discussing the plot hole than we did talking about the ending.
examples.zh: 我们讨论这个「情节漏洞」的时间比聊结局还长。

words.enDefinition: An accidental inconsistency between shots or scenes meant to show continuous action.

examples.en: I spotted a continuity error when the empty mug looked full again in the next shot.
examples.zh: 下一镜里空杯子又满了，我发现了一个「镜头衔接穿帮」。

examples.en: Our tutor replayed the scene so we could see the continuity error with the open window.
examples.zh: 导师重放那场戏，让我们看到窗户开着的那个「镜头衔接穿帮」。

words.enDefinition: An ending that leaves some outcomes or meanings for viewers to interpret.

examples.en: The open ending made us wonder whether the neighbors would ever see each other again.
examples.zh: 这个「开放式结局」让我们琢磨，那两位邻居日后还会不会再见。

examples.en: I liked the open ending because the film gave us enough clues to make up our minds.
examples.zh: 我喜欢这个「开放式结局」，因为电影给了足够的线索让我们自己判断。

words.enDefinition: An ending that feels sad and satisfying or hopeful at the same time.

examples.en: The film had a bittersweet ending when the roommates said goodbye and moved to different cities.
examples.zh: 室友们道别后搬往不同城市，电影用了个「苦乐参半的结局」。

examples.en: I kept thinking about the bittersweet ending even after we had left the cinema.
examples.zh: 离开影院后，我还一直想着那个「苦乐参半的结局」。

collocations: give a film a bittersweet ending
a film with a bittersweet ending

words.enDefinition: A story that builds interest or tension gradually over a relatively long time.

examples.en: My roommate called the series a slow burn because the big questions came much later.
examples.zh: 室友说这部剧是「慢热型作品」，因为几个大疑问到后面才抛出来。

examples.en: The film was a slow burn, but by the end I cared about every character.
examples.zh: 这部电影是「慢热型作品」，看到最后我已经很在意每个角色。

collocations: a slow burn with a strong ending
a film that is a slow burn
describe a show as a slow burn

words.enDefinition: Moving at a rate that keeps viewers engaged without making events feel rushed.

examples.en: I thought the film was well-paced because every scene revealed something about the friendship.
examples.zh: 我觉得这部电影「节奏安排得当」，每场戏都让人多了解一点这段友情。

examples.en: The documentary felt well-paced even though it gave the longer interviews time to breathe.
examples.zh: 虽然纪录片给较长的访谈留足了时间，整体仍让我觉得「节奏安排得当」。

words.enDefinition: A conversational comment that part of a story or viewing experience felt too slow.

examples.en: I enjoyed the film overall, although it dragged a bit before the final scene.
examples.zh: 整体上我喜欢这部片，不过最后一场戏之前「有点拖沓」。

examples.en: My roommate said it dragged a bit while the two friends waited for the bus.
examples.zh: 室友说，那两个朋友等公交车的那段「有点拖沓」。

collocations: it dragged a bit in the middle
it dragged a bit near the end

words.enDefinition: A film made from an earlier work such as a book, play, or comic.

examples.en: The film adaptation left out a character whom everyone in our book club remembered.
examples.zh: 这部「电影改编作品」删掉了读书会每个人都记得的一个角色。

examples.en: I watched the film adaptation the weekend I finally finished reading the novel.
examples.zh: 我终于读完小说的那个周末，就看了它的「电影改编作品」。

collocations: a film adaptation of a novel
compare a book and its film adaptation

words.enDefinition: Describes a production that draws its main narrative from events that really happened.

examples.en: The film was based on a true story about students trying to save a library.
examples.zh: 这部片「根据真实故事改编」，讲一群学生设法保住一座图书馆。

examples.en: Our class discussed which details were invented for a drama based on a true story.
examples.zh: 我们班讨论了这部「根据真实故事改编」的剧情片有哪些虚构的细节。

collocations: a film based on a true story
a series based on a true story
loosely based on a true story

words.enDefinition: A written or spoken evaluation of a film.

examples.en: I read a film review to see whether the ending was worth waiting for.
examples.zh: 我看了一篇「影评」，想知道结局值不值得等。

examples.en: Our student newspaper published a film review written by someone in my seminar group.
examples.zh: 校报发了一篇「影评」，是我们研讨小组的一位同学写的。

words.enDefinition: Good or interesting enough to justify spending the time to watch it.

examples.en: The film is worth watching just for the way the two leads play off each other.
examples.zh: 单看两位主演之间的对手戏，这部电影就「值得一看」。

examples.en: My classmate said the documentary was worth watching even if we knew the subject already.
examples.zh: 同学说，就算已经了解这个题材，这部纪录片也「值得一看」。

words.enDefinition: A performer who attracts the most attention in a scene, even in a smaller part.

examples.en: The actor playing the quiet neighbor turned out to be the scene-stealer of the film.
examples.zh: 演安静邻居的演员成了片中最「抢戏的演员」。

examples.en: One reviewer called the young actor a scene-stealer after watching the library scene twice.
examples.zh: 一位影评人看了两遍图书馆那场戏后，称这位年轻演员是「抢戏的演员」。

words.enDefinition: The recorded sound or music associated with a film, show, or other production.

examples.en: I looked up the soundtrack because I wanted to hear the opening song again.
examples.zh: 我查了这部片的「影视原声」，因为想再听一遍片头曲。

examples.en: The soundtrack got quieter just before the character opened the door to the old workshop.
examples.zh: 角色快要打开旧工作室门的时候，「影视原声」变小了。

words.enDefinition: An organized showing of a film to an audience.

examples.en: A film screening in the library brought several students from our evening class together.
examples.zh: 图书馆办了场「电影放映」，我们晚课班上的几位同学都去了。

examples.en: We checked how long the film screening would last before making plans for dinner.
examples.zh: 定晚饭安排之前，我们查了一下这场「电影放映」会持续多久。

words.enDefinition: The advertised time at which a particular movie showing is due to start.

examples.en: I checked the showtime because my class was due to finish at half past six.
examples.zh: 我那节课要到六点半才下课，所以查了「电影开场时间」。

examples.en: The latest showtime was too late for anyone who needed the last bus back.
examples.zh: 要赶末班公交回去的人觉得，最后一场的「电影开场时间」太晚了。

words.enDefinition: A showing or performance held during the day, usually in the afternoon.

examples.en: We decided on a matinee so our flatmate could come before her evening shift.
examples.zh: 我们选了「日场放映」，这样室友上晚班前能来看。

examples.en: The theater added a matinee when a group of students asked for an earlier screening.
examples.zh: 一群学生问能不能早点放，影院就加了一场「日场放映」。

words.enDefinition: A showing of a film before it is generally released to the public.

examples.en: The film society invited students to an advance screening of a documentary about public gardens.
examples.zh: 电影社邀请同学们参加一部公共花园纪录片的「提前放映」。

examples.en: My roommate had seen the film at an advance screening before it opened in town.
examples.zh: 这部片还没在城里正式上映之前，室友已在「提前放映」看过了。

collocations: an invitation to an advance screening
an advance screening of a documentary

words.enDefinition: A program in which two films are shown one after the other.

examples.en: We picked a double feature because both films were shorter than we had expected.
examples.zh: 两部片都比预想的短，我们就选了「两部电影连映」。

examples.en: There was a short break between the movies in the campus cinema's double feature.
examples.zh: 校园影院的「两部电影连映」在两片之间安排了一小段休息时间。

collocations: a double feature at the cinema

words.enDefinition: A film showing scheduled late in the evening or around midnight.

examples.en: The late-night screening ended after the last bus, so we walked back to campus.
examples.zh: 「深夜放映」结束时，末班公交已经走了，我们就步行回学校。

examples.en: I missed the late-night screening because I had a shift at the library early next morning.
examples.zh: 我第二天一早要去图书馆上班，没能去看「深夜放映」。

words.enDefinition: A film showing held outside, often with a temporary screen.

examples.en: We brought blankets to the outdoor screening because the grass was still damp after lunch.
examples.zh: 午饭后草地还是湿的，所以我们带着毯子去看「露天放映」。

examples.en: The outdoor screening moved to the covered terrace when rain began just before sunset.
examples.zh: 日落前开始下雨，「露天放映」就移到了有顶棚的露台。

collocations: an outdoor screening in the courtyard

words.enDefinition: A room set up to show films or other recorded video to an audience.

examples.en: We found the screening room just beyond the exhibition space in the arts building.
examples.zh: 我们在艺术楼的展览区过去一点找到了「放映厅」。

examples.en: The screening room was big enough for our class but much smaller than a regular cinema.
examples.zh: 「放映厅」够我们全班坐，不过比普通影院小得多。

words.enDefinition: A cinema screen, often mentioned when talking about seeing a film in a theater.

examples.en: The quiet scenes felt different on the big screen from when I watched them at home.
examples.zh: 安静的场景放到「影院大银幕」上看，感受和我在家看时不一样。

examples.en: My classmate wanted to see the animated short on the big screen at least once.
examples.zh: 同学想至少在「影院大银幕」上看一次那部动画短片。

collocations: see it on the big screen
bring a story to the big screen

words.enDefinition: The number identifying the room where a film is being shown in a cinema.

examples.en: I checked the screen number before asking which corridor led to our auditorium.
examples.zh: 我先核对了「影厅编号」，然后问走哪条走廊能到我们那一厅。

examples.en: The screen number on the digital ticket matched the sign beside the correct door.
examples.zh: 电子票上的「影厅编号」和对应门旁的标牌一致。

collocations: the screen number on the ticket

words.enDefinition: Film showings scheduled one immediately after another with little time between them.

examples.en: We missed dinner because we booked back-to-back screenings at the film festival that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚我们订了影展「紧接着的多场放映」，所以错过了晚饭。

examples.en: They scheduled back-to-back screenings of student documentaries in the small theater beside the library.
examples.zh: 他们在图书馆旁的小影院安排了学生纪录片「一场接一场放映」。

words.enDefinition: An organized event presenting a selection of films, often over several days.

examples.en: The film festival showed student shorts in the afternoon and features in the evening.
examples.zh: 「电影节」下午放学生短片，晚上放长片。

examples.en: My roommate volunteered at a film festival and brought back a copy of the program.
examples.zh: 室友去「电影节」做志愿者，带回来一份节目单。

collocations: show a film at a film festival

words.enDefinition: A question and answer session held after a film showing.

examples.en: We stayed for the post-screening Q&A because the director had filmed parts of the movie nearby.
examples.zh: 导演在附近拍了电影的一些片段，我们就留下参加了「映后问答」。

examples.en: My classmate asked about the soundtrack during the post-screening Q&A in the auditorium.
examples.zh: 同学在礼堂的「映后问答」中问到了原声音乐。

collocations: ask a question at the post-screening Q&A
a post-screening Q&A with the director

words.enDefinition: The release of a film for public showings in movie theaters.

examples.en: We waited for the theatrical release because the film was made for a large screen.
examples.zh: 这部片是为大银幕拍的，所以我们等它「院线上映」。

examples.en: The film society asked whether the documentary would get a theatrical release in our town.
examples.zh: 电影社问这部纪录片会不会在我们镇上「院线上映」。

words.enDefinition: A release in which a film is shown in a restricted number of theaters or locations.

examples.en: The film opened in limited release, and only one theater near campus was showing it.
examples.zh: 这部片「小范围上映」，校园附近只有一家影院在放。

examples.en: My roommate checked the limited release dates after hearing about the documentary in a podcast.
examples.zh: 室友在播客听说这部纪录片后，查了它「小范围上映」的日期。

words.enDefinition: A release that makes a film available in many theaters or areas at once.

examples.en: We waited for the wide release so we could see it at our local cinema.
examples.zh: 我们等到它「大范围上映」才在当地影院看。

examples.en: The student newspaper reviewed the film before its wide release across the country that month.
examples.zh: 当月这部片在全国「大范围上映」前，学生报就发了影评。

words.enDefinition: A version of a film edited according to the director's own preferred choices.

examples.en: I watched the director's cut to see how the slower opening changed the story.
examples.zh: 我看了「导演剪辑版」，想知道节奏较慢的开头让故事有什么不同。

examples.en: The campus cinema showed the director's cut as part of a program on editing.
examples.zh: 校园影院把「导演剪辑版」放进了一个有关剪辑的专题放映。

collocations: a scene from the director's cut

words.enDefinition: A version of a film that includes more material than the original release version.

examples.en: The extended cut included a longer scene in which the students moved into their flat.
examples.zh: 「加长剪辑版」里，学生们搬进公寓的那场戏更长。

examples.en: We chose the extended cut because our tutor had mentioned a scene missing from the original.
examples.zh: 导师提过原版少了一场戏，所以我们选了「加长剪辑版」。

collocations: an extended cut of a film

words.enDefinition: A later release of a previously released film, often bringing it back to theaters.

examples.en: The cinema promoted a re-release of an older comedy as part of its anniversary program.
examples.zh: 影院把一部老喜剧的「重新上映」作为周年活动来宣传。

examples.en: We missed the original screenings, so we were pleased about the re-release later that term.
examples.zh: 我们没赶上最初的场次，得知学期后面会「重新上映」很高兴。

words.enDefinition: A later broadcast of a television program that has already been shown.

examples.en: I caught a rerun of the interview while waiting for my laundry to finish.
examples.zh: 等衣服洗好时，我碰巧看到那次访谈的「重播」。

examples.en: The schedule showed a rerun at noon for anyone who missed the evening program.
examples.zh: 节目表上写着中午有「重播」，方便没看晚间节目的人补看。

collocations: a rerun of an old show

words.enDefinition: The total amount of time a film or episode runs from start to finish.

examples.en: I checked the runtime because our class needed time for discussion after the documentary.
examples.zh: 我们班看完纪录片还要留时间讨论，所以我查了「片长」。

examples.en: The runtime was listed below the synopsis in the program for the campus screening.
examples.zh: 校园放映的节目单在内容简介下面列了「片长」。

words.enDefinition: A short promotional video giving audiences a preview of an upcoming film.

examples.en: The movie trailer made the film look much faster than it actually was.
examples.zh: 「电影预告片」把这部片剪得看起来比实际节奏快得多。

examples.en: My roommate sent me a movie trailer because the cinematography reminded her of our city.
examples.zh: 室友给我发了一部「电影预告片」，因为里面的镜头让她想起我们的城市。

collocations: a movie trailer for the new film

words.enDefinition: A very brief early preview intended to create interest without revealing much about the story.

examples.en: The teaser trailer showed the location and a few faces without telling us the story.
examples.zh: 「先导预告片」只展示了地点和几张面孔，没告诉我们讲什么故事。

examples.en: Our film club watched the teaser trailer before the longer preview appeared later that month.
examples.zh: 当月晚些时候正式长预告发布前，电影社先看了「先导预告片」。

words.enDefinition: A label indicating which age groups a film or program is considered suitable for.

examples.en: We checked the age rating when a friend asked if she could bring her younger brother.
examples.zh: 朋友问能不能带弟弟来时，我们查了「观看年龄分级」。

examples.en: The campus cinema printed the age rating below each film description in its program.
examples.zh: 校园影院把「观看年龄分级」印在节目单上每部电影的简介下方。

collocations: an age rating for a film

words.enDefinition: A notice describing potentially upsetting or sensitive material in a film or program.

examples.en: The organizer read a content warning before playing the documentary in the lecture hall.
examples.zh: 纪录片在阶梯教室开播前，组织者念了一则「内容提醒」。

examples.en: I read the content warning before deciding whether to join my flatmates for the screening.
examples.zh: 和室友一起去看放映之前，我先读了「内容提醒」再决定要不要去。

words.enDefinition: Audio arranged to make sounds seem to come from several directions.

examples.en: The surround sound made it seem as though we were standing beside the river.
examples.zh: 「环绕声」让我们感觉好像就站在那条河边。

examples.en: I noticed the surround sound most during a scene with footsteps coming from behind.
examples.zh: 有一场戏里脚步声从身后传来，那时我最明显地听到了「环绕声」。

words.enDefinition: a picture format with a relatively wide aspect ratio, such as 16:9 or wider

examples.en: The widescreen format fit all three characters into the same shot in the cafe.
examples.zh: 「宽银幕画幅」让咖啡馆里的三个角色都进了同一个镜头。

examples.en: The cinema kept the original widescreen format for its showing of the restored documentary.
examples.zh: 影院放映修复后的纪录片时保留了原来的「宽银幕画幅」。

collocations: show a film in widescreen format

words.enDefinition: An online service that delivers media for playback over an internet connection.

examples.en: We checked which streaming service carried the documentary our tutor had mentioned in class.
examples.zh: 我们查了哪家「流媒体服务」可以看导师上课提过的那部纪录片。

examples.en: The streaming service offered two different versions of the film we wanted to watch.
examples.zh: 这家「流媒体服务」提供了我们想看的电影的两个不同版本。

collocations: a show on a streaming service

words.enDefinition: Describes media that people can start watching whenever they choose.

examples.en: We watched the interview on demand because most of us were working when it aired.
examples.zh: 访谈播出时我们大多数人都在上班，后来是「点播」看的。

examples.en: The documentary was available on demand after our class finished its discussion that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午课堂讨论结束后，这部纪录片就可以「点播」了。

words.enDefinition: The collection of films and shows offered by an online viewing service.

examples.en: I browsed the streaming catalog looking for a comedy short enough to watch before class.
examples.zh: 我翻了翻「流媒体片库」，想找部能在上课前看完的短喜剧。

examples.en: The streaming catalog had several documentaries from the same director under different category labels.
examples.zh: 「流媒体片库」有同一位导演的几部纪录片，放在不同的分类下面。

collocations: add a film to the streaming catalog

words.enDefinition: Offered for online playback through a streaming service.

examples.en: The film was available to stream with subtitles, so our whole group could follow it.
examples.zh: 那部片「可在线播放」，还带字幕，因此我们整个小组都能看懂。

examples.en: We checked whether the short was available to stream after missing the screening on campus.
examples.zh: 错过学校的放映后，我们查了这部短片是否「可在线播放」。

collocations: check what is available to stream

words.enDefinition: A film or show produced or commissioned specifically for a streaming service.

examples.en: The film club chose a streaming original for its discussion about how series are made.
examples.zh: 电影社选了一部「流媒体原创作品」，用来讨论剧集是怎么制作的。

examples.en: My classmate recommended a streaming original that had been filmed in her hometown that summer.
examples.zh: 同学推荐了一部「流媒体原创作品」，是那个夏天在她家乡拍的。

words.enDefinition: To watch many episodes of a series in one sitting or over a short period.

examples.en: We decided to binge-watch the series after handing in our last assignment of the term.
examples.zh: 交完这学期最后一份作业后，我们决定把这部剧「一口气连看多集」。

examples.en: I meant to watch one episode and ended up staying in to binge-watch the entire season.
examples.zh: 我原本只想看一集，最后留在家里把整季「一口气看完」了。

words.enDefinition: To watch the episodes you have missed so that you are up to date.

examples.en: I used the long weekend to catch up on a series my roommates were already discussing.
examples.zh: 我趁小长假把那部剧「补看」完，室友们已经在讨论它了。

examples.en: My friend wanted to catch up on a series before joining our lunchtime discussion about it.
examples.zh: 朋友想先「补看落下的剧集」，再参加我们午饭时的讨论。

collocations: try to catch up on a series
take the weekend to catch up on a series
find time to catch up on a series

words.enDefinition: A saved list of films or shows someone intends to watch.

examples.en: I added the short film to my watchlist because I had to leave for class.
examples.zh: 我得出门上课了，就把那部短片加进了「待看片单」。

examples.en: My roommate looked through her watchlist for something we could finish before the last bus.
examples.zh: 室友翻了翻她的「待看片单」，想找部赶末班公交前能看完的片子。

collocations: add a film to your watchlist
remove a title from the watchlist

words.enDefinition: A player or service label for items someone has started and can pick back up.

examples.en: The film appeared in the “Continue Watching” row when we came back from our evening class.
examples.zh: 我们上完晚课回来时，这部片出现在「继续观看栏」。

examples.en: I opened “Continue Watching” to find the episode we had started the night before.
examples.zh: 我打开「继续观看栏」，找前一天晚上开始看的那一集。

words.enDefinition: To start a paused or stopped video again from the position already reached.

examples.en: I pressed the button to resume playback after my roommate came back with tea.
examples.zh: 室友拿着茶回来后，我按了按钮「恢复播放」。

examples.en: Could you resume playback now that everyone is back from the kitchen with snacks?
examples.zh: 大家已经从厨房拿完零食回来了，你能「恢复播放」吗？

words.enDefinition: To start a selected film or episode at its opening again.

examples.en: I chose “Play from the beginning” because my flatmate had missed the opening scene.
examples.zh: 室友没看到开场戏，所以我选了「从头播放」。

examples.en: The player let us play from the beginning without having to reload the whole film.
examples.zh: 播放器让我们不用重新载入整部电影，就可以「从头播放」。

collocations: a play from the beginning option

words.enDefinition: A player control for moving past a show's opening title or theme sequence.

examples.en: We used “Skip intro” after watching the opening credits in the first episode that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚看过第一集的片头后，我们用了「跳过片头」。

examples.en: The skip intro button appeared as soon as the familiar theme music started playing.
examples.zh: 熟悉的主题音乐一响起，「跳过片头」按钮就出现了。

words.enDefinition: A brief summary of events from earlier episodes, often shown before a new episode.

examples.en: The episode recap reminded us why the main character had decided to leave town.
examples.zh: 「前情回顾」让我们想起主角为什么决定离开小镇。

examples.en: My roommate asked for a quick episode recap when she realized she had missed last week's show.
examples.zh: 室友发现没看上周那集，就请我简单做个「前情回顾」。

words.enDefinition: A setting that starts the following episode automatically when one episode finishes.

examples.en: I turned off “Autoplay next episode” because we had agreed to finish after one more.
examples.zh: 我们说好再看一集就结束，所以我关了「自动播放下一集」。

examples.en: My classmate found the autoplay next episode setting while looking for the subtitle controls.
examples.zh: 同学在找字幕设置时，发现了「自动播放下一集」选项。

words.enDefinition: A release schedule in which new episodes become available once a week.

examples.en: The weekly release gave our friends time to talk about each episode before the next one.
examples.zh: 「按周更新」让朋友们有时间在下一集出来前聊聊这一集。

examples.en: I prefer a weekly release when several people are trying to watch the same show together.
examples.zh: 好几个人想一起追同一部剧时，我更喜欢「按周更新」。

words.enDefinition: An informal way to say the next episode becomes available to watch.

examples.en: My roommate asked when the next episode drops so we could arrange to watch it together.
examples.zh: 室友问「下一集什么时候上线」，好约个时间一起看。

examples.en: We decided to leave the discussion until the next episode drops at the weekend.
examples.zh: 我们决定等周末「下一集上线」时再讨论。

collocations: the next episode drops on Friday
ask when the next episode drops
wait until the next episode drops

words.enDefinition: A label grouping titles that have been added to a service in the recent past.

examples.en: I found an old documentary under “Recently added” while looking for something short to watch.
examples.zh: 我想找部短点的片子时，在「近期加入片库」一栏发现了一部老纪录片。

examples.en: The recently added section included a film that my class had watched a year earlier.
examples.zh: 「近期加入片库」栏目里有一部我们班一年前看过的电影。

words.enDefinition: A label warning that a title will soon stop being available on the service.

examples.en: The film had a “Leaving soon” label, so we watched it that evening after class.
examples.zh: 这部片标着「即将下架」，我们当晚下课后就把它看了。

examples.en: I looked in the leaving soon section to see whether the documentary was still available.
examples.zh: 我去「即将下架」栏目查了查那部纪录片还能不能看。

words.enDefinition: To save a video on a device so it can be watched without internet access.

examples.en: I chose to download for offline viewing before taking the train home for the weekend.
examples.zh: 周末坐火车回家前，我选了「下载后离线观看」。

examples.en: The app displayed “Download for offline viewing” beneath some of the films on my list.
examples.zh: 应用在我清单里部分电影的下方显示了「下载后离线观看」。

collocations: an option to download for offline viewing
choose to download for offline viewing

words.enDefinition: A program transmitted for audiences to watch or listen to as the event happens.

examples.en: We watched a live broadcast of the film awards in the lounge after class.
examples.zh: 下课后，我们在休息室看了电影颁奖典礼的「现场直播」。

examples.en: My flatmate stayed up for the live broadcast because she wanted to hear the interviews.
examples.zh: 室友想听访谈，所以熬夜等着看「现场直播」。

collocations: a live broadcast of the ceremony

words.enDefinition: To repeatedly pause while waiting for more content to load for playback.

examples.en: Videos keep buffering in the lounge, but the same film played in my room.
examples.zh: 公共休息室里的视频「不断缓冲」，同一部片在我房间却能播。

examples.en: Why does it keep buffering just as the music starts in the opening scene?
examples.zh: 怎么开场戏音乐刚响，就开始「不断缓冲」了？

words.enDefinition: To watch or deliver a video stream at high-definition picture quality.

examples.en: We chose to stream in HD when the details in the landscape mattered to us.
examples.zh: 风景细节对我们很重要，所以我们选了「以高清画质在线播放」。

examples.en: I checked whether we could stream in HD on the screen in our common room.
examples.zh: 我查了公共休息室的屏幕能不能「以高清画质在线播放」。

collocations: an option to stream in HD

words.enDefinition: A separate recorded sound option that can be played with a video.

examples.en: I selected a different audio track because our guests wanted to hear the original voices.
examples.zh: 来做客的朋友想听原来的声音，我就换了一条「音轨」。

examples.en: The school archive listed the language of each audio track beside the restored film.
examples.zh: 学校档案馆在修复过的电影旁列出了每条「音轨」的语言。

words.enDefinition: The sound track containing the production’s original recorded dialogue and audio.

examples.en: We chose the original audio so we could hear how the actors delivered their lines.
examples.zh: 我们选了「原声音轨」，想听演员原本怎么说台词。

examples.en: The original audio was available in the menu beside two other language tracks for the film.
examples.zh: 菜单里有这部电影的「原声音轨」，旁边还有两条其他语言的音轨。

collocations: play a film with the original audio

words.enDefinition: A version with the original dialogue replaced by newly recorded speech, often in another language.

examples.en: My roommate chose the dubbed version so her little brother could follow the story.
examples.zh: 室友选了「配音版」，好让弟弟能跟上故事。

examples.en: We compared the dubbed version with the original because the jokes sounded different in translation.
examples.zh: 译过来的笑话听起来不一样，我们就把「配音版」和原版作了比较。

words.enDefinition: A version presented with written subtitles alongside the spoken dialogue.

examples.en: The cinema showed a subtitled version of the comedy for students in our language class.
examples.zh: 影院给我们语言班的同学放了那部喜剧的「字幕版」。

examples.en: I chose the subtitled version because I liked hearing the actors' voices in the film.
examples.zh: 我喜欢听片中演员本来的声音，就选了「字幕版」。

words.enDefinition: The language in which the subtitles are displayed.

examples.en: I changed the subtitle language so my visiting cousin could follow what people were saying.
examples.zh: 我换了「字幕语言」，方便来做客的表亲看懂人物在说什么。

examples.en: The menu let us choose the subtitle language while keeping the same audio track.
examples.zh: 菜单允许我们选「字幕语言」，同时保留原先那条音轨。

words.enDefinition: captions for speech and relevant sounds that stay on screen and cannot be switched off

examples.en: The film society arranged a screening with open captions in the arts building that evening.
examples.zh: 电影社那晚在艺术楼安排了一场带「常显无障碍字幕」的放映。

examples.en: The open captions identified the offscreen speaker and described the music before the scene changed.
examples.zh: 场景切换前，「常显无障碍字幕」标明了画外说话者，还描述了音乐。

collocations: show a film with open captions

words.enDefinition: Spoken narration that conveys important visual information for people who cannot see it clearly.

examples.en: The audio description told us what appeared on the sign between the lines of dialogue.
examples.zh: 两句台词之间，「口述影像」说明了标牌上出现的内容。

examples.en: Our campus cinema listed audio description alongside the other accessibility options in the program.
examples.zh: 校园影院在节目单上把「口述影像」和其他无障碍选项列在一起。

words.enDefinition: Describes subtitles that appear before or after the matching speech or sound.

examples.en: I noticed the subtitles were out of sync when the characters started talking over dinner.
examples.zh: 角色们刚在晚饭时聊起来，我发现「字幕与音频不同步」。

examples.en: The menu was slow to open, and the subtitles were out of sync again.
examples.zh: 菜单打开得很慢，而且「字幕与音频不同步」的问题又出现了。

collocations: notice the subtitles are out of sync
the subtitles were slightly out of sync
subtitles out of sync with the dialogue

words.enDefinition: Presenting a wide picture on a narrower screen with bars above and below the image.

examples.en: The film used letterboxing to keep its wide picture visible on our older television.
examples.zh: 这部片用「宽画面上下留黑边」的方式，让老电视也能显示整个宽画面。

examples.en: Our tutor explained letterboxing when we noticed black bars above and below the film.
examples.zh: 我们发现电影画面上下的黑边时，导师讲了「宽画面上下留黑边」这种做法。

words.enDefinition: A notice saying a title is not offered for viewing in the viewer's location.

examples.en: The site showed “Unavailable in your region” when I looked up the documentary after class.
examples.zh: 下课后我查那部纪录片时，网站显示「所在地区无法观看」。

examples.en: I saw “Unavailable in your region” beside a title my cousin had recommended from abroad.
examples.zh: 我在国外表亲推荐的那部作品旁看到了「所在地区无法观看」。

collocations: a message saying unavailable in your region
a title marked unavailable in your region
